name: ViewerToolbar
intent: Control bar for a FragmentViewer: navigation (orbit/pan), fit, select, ortho, clipping sections, the four measurement tools, an IFC storey menu, hide/isolate/show-all, and an appearance menu carrying ghost mode and shading. Chrome only — it reads and drives viewer state through context and owns no 3D code. Stays on one row as long as it fits, dropping labels before it wraps.
when: A FragmentViewer needs the controls a BIM viewer is expected to have
The host wants to place viewer controls independently of the canvas
whenNot: There is no FragmentViewerProvider in the tree — the hook throws by design
Only one or two actions are needed -> call the useFragmentViewer() API directly from your own buttons

chooseOver.component: Building buttons against the That Open SDK directly
chooseOver.because: ViewerToolbar keeps engine wiring in one place and renders entirely from Core components, so it themes with the rest of the product.

allowedPlacement: beside or floating over a FragmentViewer, inside its FragmentViewerProvider
forbiddenPlacement: as a general-purpose application toolbar -> use Toolbar
commonMistakes: Wrapping it in a content-sized box: the bar measures its nearest positioned ancestor to pick its density, so a shrink-to-fit wrapper makes that measurement circular. Give it a full-width positioned ancestor.
Pairing pointer-events:none on a wrapper with pointer-events-auto on the bar — if the host's Tailwind hasn't emitted that utility, every click is silently swallowed
Placing it over the bottom-left of the canvas, where the That Open SDK draws its logo
Expecting a tool button to act immediately: Sections and Measure arm a tool, then a click in the viewport places the plane or point

derivedFrom.source: BIMCamel's viewer toolbar as the reference layout; behaviour from @thatopen/components + components-front
extracted: navigation mode / fit / select / ortho group
sections and the four measurement tools
panel switches for Levels, Appearance, Props, Model

notes: chrome only: every button calls the viewer API from context, so this file contains no 3D code
Levels and Appearance are menus; Props has no button — the host shows it as selection arrives
Pan is not an SDK navigation mode: it is Orbit with the left mouse button set to truck
ghost mode swaps Fragments materials directly; the SDK has no component for it
